summary: The appointment with a string on it: {appointer} tells you that your run for {the office} costs you the board seat they gave you.
realLife: In 1976 Mayor George Moscone appointed him to San Francisco's Board of Permit Appeals; weeks later he announced for the state Assembly against the mayor's choice and was removed, which he said made him the underdog.
gates: You hold an appointed board seat.
You filed or announced for an office where {appointer} backs someone else.
weights: How much the race matters to you.
choices: ask for time and tell no one

branches.then: It is in the paper next morning. You can run on being the underdog or say nothing.
{appointer} offers a better post after the election if you sit this one out, a promise on both records.
{appointer} asks how you will vote on a permit they care about, and the answer shows what you will trade.
